final_answer.key_evidence_summary: 14 services in namespace train-ticket are in CrashLoopBackOff (RESTARTS 10) across worker-01/02/03, so this is not a node-scope fault. Their error logs all show the identical startup failure: 'java.sql.SQLNonTransientConnectionException: Too many connections' / 'SQL Error: 1040, SQLState: 08004' during 'HikariPool-1 - Exception during pool initialization', leading to 'Unable to build Hibernate SessionFactory' and 'Application run failed'. The database side confirms the mechanism: tsdb-mysql error logs contain 1506 occurrences of '[Warning] Too many connections' (error ratio 0.57) while its mysqld process and replication stay up, and the events surface binds the mechanism verbatim to the DB instance: 'Warning Unhealthy pod/tsdb-mysql-0 Readiness probe failed: ERROR 1040 (HY000): Too many connections', alongside 'Warning BackOff ... Back-off restarting failed container <svc>' rows for each crashing service. All other event rows are Normal (Scheduled/Created/Started/Pulled), ruling out scheduling, image-pull, mount and probe-config causes. tsdb-mysql is the shared MySQL behind the data services (StatefulSet 3 replicas, ConfigMap node.cnf), so the connection slots of the database were exhausted and every new application connection pool was rejected at startup.

      if [ $i = 0 ]

        echo -n "tsdb-mysql-${i}.tsdb-mysql.train-ticket:8801"

    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    curl -X PATCH -H "Authorization: Bearer $(cat /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token)" -H "Content-Type: application/json-patch+json" \
    --cacert /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/ca.crt https://$KUBERNETES_SERVICE_HOST:$KUBERNETES_PORT_443_TCP_PORT/api/v1/namespaces/train-ticket/pods/$HOSTNAME \

    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    curl -X PATCH -H "Authorization: Bearer $(cat /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token)" -H "Content-Type: application/json-patch+json" \
